📚 PART 2: DETAILED CONTENT

🟢 TOPIC 1: EC2 BASICS

📋 What to Learn

ConceptKey Point
What is EC2?Virtual servers (IaaS) in AWS
Service modelIaaS — you manage OS + apps
BillingPer-second (Linux), per-hour (some Windows)
Global reachRegion → AZ → Instance

📖 Content

EC2 = Elastic Compute Cloud = Rent virtual servers on AWS.

  • You choose: OS, CPU, RAM, storage, network
  • You manage: OS patches, apps, security
  • AWS manages: hardware, hypervisor, data center

🎯 Exam Tip: EC2 is IaaS, not PaaS/SaaS.

🔴 TOPIC 2: INSTANCE TYPES

📋 What to Learn

FamilyTypeExam Keyword
TBurstable GeneralLow traffic, bursty, dev/test
MGeneral PurposeBalanced workload
CCompute OptimizedCPU-intensive, HPC, batch
RMemory OptimizedIn-memory DB, Redis
XExtreme MemorySAP HANA, massive RAM
IStorage (NVMe SSD)High IOPS, NoSQL
DStorage (HDD)Hadoop, data warehouse
PGPU – TrainingML training, deep learning
GGPU – GraphicsVideo, rendering, gaming
InfInferenceML inference
TrnTrainingCost-effective ML training
g (suffix)Graviton ARMBest price/performance

📖 Content

🔸 T-Family (Burstable)

  • Baseline CPU + CPU credits for bursts
  • T3 Standard = throttle when credits run out
  • T3 Unlimited = pay extra to keep bursting
  • Use: Dev/test, small blogs, low-traffic APIs

🔸 M-Family (General Purpose)

  • Balanced CPU:memory ratio
  • Use: Web apps, small DBs, enterprise apps

🔸 C-Family (Compute Optimized)

  • High CPU, less RAM
  • Use: Batch processing, video encoding, gaming servers, HPC, scientific computing

🔸 R-Family (Memory Optimized)

  • High RAM
  • Use: Redis, Memcached, Elasticsearch, large DBs

🔸 X-Family (Extreme Memory)

  • Up to 24 TB RAM
  • Use: SAP HANA, massive in-memory databases

🔸 I-Family (NVMe Storage)

  • Local SSDs, ultra-high IOPS
  • Use: Cassandra, MongoDB, NoSQL, transactional DBs

🔸 D-Family (HDD Storage)

  • Huge HDD capacity (up to 336 TB)
  • Use: Hadoop, HDFS, data lakes

🔸 P-Family (GPU Training)

  • NVIDIA V100/A100/H100 GPUs
  • Use: Deep learning, LLM training

🔸 G-Family (GPU Graphics)

  • Cheaper GPUs
  • Use: Video rendering, 3D, game streaming, ML inference

🔸 Inf / Trn (AWS Custom Chips)

  • Inf = Inference; Trn = Training
  • Use: Cost-effective ML workloads

🔸 Graviton (ARM — "g" suffix)

  • AWS's ARM chip, 40% better price/performance
  • Use: Cost optimization for recompiled apps

🔴 TOPIC 3: PRICING MODELS

📋 What to Learn

ModelDiscountCommitmentInterruption
On-Demand0%NoneNo
Reserved Standard72%1 or 3 yrNo
Reserved Convertible54%1 or 3 yrNo
Compute Savings Plan66%1 or 3 yrNo
EC2 Instance Savings Plan72%1 or 3 yrNo
Spot90%NoneYes (2-min warning)
Dedicated HostCostlyOptionalNo
Dedicated InstanceCostlyNoneNo
Capacity Reservation0%NoneNo

📖 Content

🔸 On-Demand

  • Pay per use, no commitment
  • Use: Short-term, unpredictable

🔸 Reserved Instance (RI) — Standard

  • Commit 1 or 3 years, 72% off
  • Use: 24/7 production (DBs, AD, API servers)

🔸 Reserved Instance — Convertible

  • Can change family/OS/tenancy later
  • Use: Long commitment with architectural flexibility

🔸 Compute Savings Plan

  • Commit $/hr across EC2 + Lambda + Fargate
  • Flexible across regions/families
  • Use: Multi-service workloads

🔸 EC2 Instance Savings Plan

  • Commit to specific family in specific region
  • Flexible on size, AZ, OS
  • Use: Known family, variable size

🔸 Spot

  • Up to 90% off, can be interrupted
  • Use: Batch jobs, ML training, CI/CD, big data
  • NEVER: Production DBs, stateful apps

🔸 Dedicated Host

  • Entire physical server
  • See sockets/cores for BYOL licenses
  • Use: Oracle, SQL Server, Windows BYOL

🔸 Dedicated Instance

  • Hardware isolated but no socket visibility
  • Use: Isolation for compliance (no license concern)

🔸 Capacity Reservation

  • Reserve capacity in an AZ, no discount
  • Use: Guarantee capacity for events (Black Friday)

🎯 Decision Triggers

KeywordPick
"Interruptible / batch"Spot
"Always running"Reserved
"Flexible across services"Compute Savings Plan
"BYOL / license audit"Dedicated Host
"Guarantee capacity"Capacity Reservation

🔴 TOPIC 4: STORAGE – EBS

📋 What to Learn

Volume TypeMax IOPSUse Case
gp316,000Default, cost-effective
gp216,000Legacy (IOPS tied to size)
io2 Block Express256,000SAP HANA, highest performance
io1 / io264,000High-perf DB, Multi-Attach
st1500Big data, sequential HDD
sc1250Cold, cheapest HDD

📖 Content

🔸 EBS Fundamentals

  • Network-attached block storage (virtual hard drive)
  • AZ-locked — lives in ONE AZ
  • Persistent — survives instance stop
  • Attach/detach to another EC2 (same AZ)

🔸 gp3

  • New default — decouples IOPS from size
  • 20% cheaper than gp2

🔸 io2 Block Express

  • 256,000 IOPS, sub-ms latency
  • 99.999% durability
  • Use: SAP HANA, mission-critical DBs

🔸 io1/io2 Multi-Attach

  • Up to 16 Nitro instances attach to same volume
  • Same AZ only
  • Requires cluster-aware file system
  • Use: Oracle RAC, clustered apps

🔸 Snapshots

  • Stored in S3 (managed by AWS)
  • Incremental — only changed blocks
  • Copy across regions for DR
  • Create AMI from snapshot

🔸 Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR)

  • Pre-warms volumes from snapshot
  • Full performance immediately
  • Use: Low-RTO disaster recovery

🔸 Encryption

  • Uses KMS
  • Encrypt unencrypted volume: snapshot → copy (encrypted) → restore

⚠️ Key Facts

  1. EBS is AZ-locked
  2. Snapshots stored in S3
  3. Multi-Attach = io1/io2 only
  4. Delete on Termination = ON for root, OFF for additional

🟡 TOPIC 5: STORAGE – INSTANCE STORE

📋 What to Learn

PropertyBehavior
AttachedPhysical host
SpeedUltra-fast (NVMe)
PersistenceLOST on stop/terminate/hibernate
Survives reboot?✅ Yes

📖 Content

  • Ephemeral SSDs on host
  • Use: Cache, buffer, scratch data, temp processing
  • App must replicate data elsewhere (Cassandra, Kafka)

🎯 Exam Trap: "Data lost on stop" = Instance Store

🔴 TOPIC 6: STORAGE – EFS & FSx

📋 What to Learn

ServiceProtocolOSUse Case
EFSNFSLinuxShared multi-AZ Linux FS
FSx for WindowsSMBWindowsAD-integrated file share
FSx for LustreLustreLinuxHPC, ML, genomics
FSx for ONTAPMultiMultiNetApp migration

📖 Content

🔸 EFS (Elastic File System)

  • NFS v4, Linux only
  • Multi-AZ, scales automatically
  • Shared by thousands of EC2s
  • Pay per GB used
  • Storage classes: Standard, IA, One Zone
  • Use: WordPress fleet, shared CMS, container storage

🔸 FSx for Windows

  • SMB, Windows-native
  • AD integration, DFS namespaces
  • Use: Windows file shares, .NET apps, SharePoint

🔸 FSx for Lustre

  • Sub-ms latency, 100s GB/s throughput
  • Integrates with S3
  • Use: ML training, HPC, genomics, rendering

🔸 FSx for ONTAP / OpenZFS

  • Enterprise NAS, multi-protocol
  • Use: NetApp migrations

🟡 TOPIC 7: AMI

📋 What to Learn

ConceptDetail
DefinitionOS + apps + config template
ScopeRegion-specific
TypesAWS, Marketplace, Community, Custom
BackingEBS-backed (can stop) / Instance Store-backed (cannot stop)

📖 Content

  • Custom AMI = snapshot + launch permissions + metadata
  • Copy AMI to another region for DR/global deployment
  • EC2 Image Builder = automated AMI pipeline (create → test → distribute)

🎯 Exam Trap: AMIs are region-scoped → must copy for another region.

🔴 TOPIC 8: SECURITY – SG vs NACL

📋 What to Learn

FeatureSecurity GroupNACL
LevelInstanceSubnet
Stateful?✅ Yes❌ No
RulesAllow onlyAllow + Deny
DefaultDeny inbound, allow outboundAllow all

📖 Content

🔸 Security Group (SG)

  • Virtual firewall at instance/ENI level
  • Stateful — response auto-allowed
  • Can reference other SGs (not just IPs)

🔸 NACL

  • Firewall at subnet level
  • Stateless — must allow in AND out
  • Rules numbered (lowest first)
  • Supports Deny rules

🎯 Pick the Right One

  • Block specific IP → NACL (SG can't deny)
  • Allow web tier → app tier → SG referencing SG
  • Extra compliance layer → NACL

🟡 TOPIC 9: SECURITY – IAM ROLE & IMDS

📋 What to Learn

ConceptKey Point
IAM RoleAttach via Instance Profile
IMDSv1Simple GET (vulnerable to SSRF)
IMDSv2Token-based (secure)

📖 Content

  • NEVER hardcode access keys
  • Apps on EC2 auto-fetch credentials from IMDS
  • Always enforce IMDSv2 → prevents SSRF attacks

🟡 TOPIC 10: SECURITY – SESSION MANAGER

📋 What to Learn

FeatureBenefit
No port 22No SSH keys
No bastionDirect secure access
Logs to CloudWatch/S3Full audit trail
Works in private subnetNo public IP needed

📖 Content

AWS Systems Manager Session Manager = browser/CLI shell to EC2.

  • Zero-trust architecture
  • Eliminates bastion hosts
  • Compliance-friendly

🔴 TOPIC 11: LOAD BALANCERS

📋 What to Learn

LBLayerPick When
ALB7 (HTTP)Path/host routing, microservices
NLB4 (TCP/UDP)Static IP, ultra-low latency, UDP
GLB33rd-party firewall/IDS
CLBLegacy❌ Avoid

📖 Content

🔸 ALB (Application Load Balancer)

  • Path, host, header, query routing
  • WebSocket, HTTP/2, gRPC
  • Targets: Instance, IP, Lambda, ALB
  • Sticky sessions, SNI, HTTP→HTTPS redirect
  • Use: Microservices, containers (ECS/EKS)

🔸 NLB (Network Load Balancer)

  • Millions req/sec, 100 μs latency
  • Static IP per AZ (can attach EIP)
  • Preserves source IP natively
  • TCP, UDP, TLS
  • Use: Gaming, IoT, trading, whitelisted IPs

🔸 GLB (Gateway Load Balancer)

  • GENEVE protocol, transparent inspection
  • Use: Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point in AWS

🎯 Triggers

KeywordPick
"Static IP"NLB
"Path routing"ALB
"UDP"NLB
"Lambda target"ALB
"Firewall inspection"GLB

🔴 TOPIC 12: AUTO SCALING GROUP (ASG)

📋 What to Learn

PolicyWhen to Use
Target Tracking"Keep CPU at 50%" (simplest)
Step ScalingMulti-threshold
ScheduledKnown time (9 AM rush)
PredictiveML-forecast patterns

📖 Content

🔸 Components

  • Launch Template (preferred) — versioned, supports Spot
  • Min / Desired / Max capacity
  • Health checks (EC2 or ELB)
  • Multi-AZ distribution

🔸 Lifecycle Hooks

  • Run scripts before instance serves traffic
  • Use: Install agents, bootstrap, register with discovery

🔸 Warm Pool

  • Pre-initialized stopped instances
  • Use: Fast scale-out for sudden bursts

🔸 Mixed Instances Policy

  • On-Demand base + Spot for cost savings
  • Multiple instance types for availability

🎯 Key Facts

  • ASG is FREE — pay only EC2
  • Launch Template > Launch Configuration
  • Target Tracking is the simplest/recommended policy

🟡 TOPIC 13: PLACEMENT GROUPS

📋 What to Learn

TypePlacementUse Case
ClusterSame rack, same AZHPC, low latency
SpreadDistinct hardwareCritical small clusters (max 7/AZ)
PartitionSeparate racks per partitionBig data (Hadoop, Kafka, Cassandra)

📖 Content

🔸 Cluster

  • Lowest latency (< 1 ms)
  • Highest PPS
  • Use: HPC, distributed ML with EFA

🔸 Spread

  • Max 7 instances per AZ
  • Each on distinct hardware
  • Use: Critical domain controllers, master nodes

🔸 Partition

  • Up to 7 partitions per AZ
  • Use: HDFS, Kafka, Cassandra (rack-aware replication)

🟡 TOPIC 14: NETWORKING – IP

📋 What to Learn

IP TypeBehavior
PrivatePermanent, free
PublicChanges on stop/start
Elastic IP (EIP)Static, charged if unused

📖 Content

  • Use EIP when you need fixed public IP
  • Limit: 5 EIPs/region (soft)
  • Best practice: Prefer ALB/NLB + Route 53 over EIP for HA

🟡 TOPIC 15: NETWORKING – ENI / ENA / EFA

📋 What to Learn

ComponentPurpose
ENIVirtual NIC
ENAEnhanced networking (100+ Gbps)
EFAOS-bypass for HPC/MPI/NCCL

📖 Content

🔸 ENI (Elastic Network Interface)

  • Virtual NIC — attach/detach from instances
  • Moves IP + MAC + SGs together
  • Use: IP failover, multi-homed EC2, MAC-tied licensing

🔸 ENA (Elastic Network Adapter)

  • Up to 100+ Gbps
  • Default on Nitro instances
  • Use: High-throughput workloads

🔸 EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter)

  • ENA + OS-bypass (via Libfabric)
  • Supports MPI, NCCL
  • Same AZ only, Cluster PG recommended
  • Use: HPC, distributed ML training

🟡 TOPIC 16: NAT GATEWAY

📋 What to Learn

ConceptKey Point
PurposeOutbound internet for private subnets
ScopePer-AZ
HADeploy one per AZ
ThroughputUp to 45 Gbps

📖 Content

  • Managed NAT for private subnet outbound traffic
  • Single NAT GW = single-AZ failure risk
  • 🎯 Exam Trap: Always one NAT GW per AZ for HA

🟡 TOPIC 17: INSTANCE LIFECYCLE

📋 What to Learn

ActionEBSRAMInstance StoreBilling
RebootKeptKeptKeptContinues
StopKeptLostLOSTEBS only
HibernateKeptSaved to EBSLOSTEBS + EIP
TerminateDeleted*LostLOSTStops

📖 Content

🔸 Hibernation Requirements

  • Nitro-based instance
  • EBS root, encrypted
  • RAM ≤ 150 GB
  • Supported OS (Amazon Linux 2, Ubuntu, Windows)

Use Case: Apps with long warm-up (ML models, caches, JVMs) — pause overnight, resume fast.

🔴 TOPIC 18: MONITORING (CloudWatch)

📋 What to Learn

MetricDefault?
CPU✅ Yes
Network✅ Yes
Disk I/O✅ Yes
Status Checks✅ Yes
Memory (RAM)❌ Needs Agent
Disk space used❌ Needs Agent
Process metrics❌ Needs Agent

📖 Content

🔸 Status Checks

TypeFailure =Fix
SystemAWS infra issueStop/Start (moves host)
InstanceYour OS/configYou fix it

🔸 EC2 Auto-Recovery

  • CloudWatch alarm on system check → auto-recover
  • Preserves instance ID, IP, metadata

⚠️ Classic Exam Trap

"How to monitor RAM?" → Install CloudWatch Agent (not default!)

🟡 TOPIC 19: DISASTER RECOVERY

📋 What to Learn

StrategyRTOCost
Backup & RestoreHours💰
Pilot Light10s of mins💰💰
Warm StandbyMinutes💰💰💰
Multi-Site Active/ActiveSeconds💰💰💰💰

📖 Content

🔸 Backup & Restore

  • Snapshots copied to DR region
  • Cheapest, highest RTO

🔸 Pilot Light

  • Core DB replicated always
  • Scale up web tier during DR

🔸 Warm Standby

  • Full DR running scaled-down
  • Scale up during disaster

🔸 Multi-Site Active/Active

  • Full prod in multiple regions
  • Route 53 weighted/failover
  • Most expensive, near-zero downtime

Can change family/OS/tenancy later
Use: Long commitment with architectural flexibility
🔸 Compute Savings Plan
Commit $/hr across EC2 + Lambda + Fargate
Flexible across regions/families
Use: Multi-service workloads
🔸 EC2 Instance Savings Plan
Commit to specific family in specific region
Flexible on size, AZ, OS
Use: Known family, variable size
🔸 Spot
Up to 90% off, can be interrupted
Use: Batch jobs, ML training, CI/CD, big data
NEVER: Production DBs, stateful apps
🔸 Dedicated Host
Entire physical server
See sockets/cores for BYOL licenses
Use: Oracle, SQL Server, Windows BYOL
🔸 Dedicated Instance
Hardware isolated but no socket visibility
Use: Isolation for compliance (no license concern)
🔸 Capacity Reservation
Reserve capacity in an AZ, no discount
Use: Guarantee capacity for events (Black Friday)
🎯 Decision Triggers
KEYWORD	PICK
"Interruptible / batch"	Spot
"Always running"	Reserved
"Flexible across services"	Compute Savings Plan
"BYOL / license audit"	Dedicated Host
"Guarantee capacity"	Capacity Reservation
🔴 TOPIC 4: STORAGE – EBS
📋 What to Learn
VOLUME TYPE	MAX IOPS	USE CASE
gp3	16,000	Default, cost-effective
gp2	16,000	Legacy (IOPS tied to size)
io2 Block Express	256,000	SAP HANA, highest performance
io1 / io2	64,000	High-perf DB, Multi-Attach
st1	500	Big data, sequential HDD
sc1	250	Cold, cheapest HDD
📖 Content
🔸 EBS Fundamentals
Network-attached block storage (virtual hard drive)
AZ-locked — lives in ONE AZ
Persistent — survives instance stop
Attach/detach to another EC2 (same AZ)
🔸 gp3
New default — decouples IOPS from size
20% cheaper than gp2
🔸 io2 Block Express
256,000 IOPS, sub-ms latency
99.999% durability
Use: SAP HANA, mission-critical DBs
🔸 io1/io2 Multi-Attach
Up to 16 Nitro instances attach to same volume
Same AZ only
Requires cluster-aware file system
Use: Oracle RAC, clustered apps
🔸 Snapshots
Stored in S3 (managed by AWS)
Incremental — only changed blocks
Copy across regions for DR
Create AMI from snapshot
🔸 Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR)
Pre-warms volumes from snapshot
Full performance immediately
Use: Low-RTO disaster recovery
🔸 Encryption
Uses KMS
Encrypt unencrypted volume: snapshot → copy (encrypted) → restore
⚠️ Key Facts
EBS is AZ-locked
Snapshots stored in S3
Multi-Attach = io1/io2 only
Delete on Termination = ON for root, OFF for additional
🟡 TOPIC 5: STORAGE – INSTANCE STORE
📋 What to Learn
PROPERTY	BEHAVIOR
Attached	Physical host
Speed	Ultra-fast (NVMe)
Persistence	LOST on stop/terminate/hibernate

📖 Content
Ephemeral SSDs on host
Use: Cache, buffer, scratch data, temp processing
App must replicate data elsewhere (Cassandra, Kafka)

📖 Content
🔸 EFS (Elastic File System)
NFS v4, Linux only
Multi-AZ, scales automatically
Shared by thousands of EC2s
Pay per GB used
Storage classes: Standard, IA, One Zone
Use: WordPress fleet, shared CMS, container storage
🔸 FSx for Windows
SMB, Windows-native
AD integration, DFS namespaces
Use: Windows file shares, .NET apps, SharePoint
🔸 FSx for Lustre
Sub-ms latency, 100s GB/s throughput
Integrates with S3
Use: ML training, HPC, genomics, rendering
🔸 FSx for ONTAP / OpenZFS
Enterprise NAS, multi-protocol

🟡 TOPIC 7: AMI
📋 What to Learn
CONCEPT	DETAIL

Scope	Region-specific
Types	AWS, Marketplace, Community, Custom

Custom AMI = snapshot + launch permissions + metadata

EC2 Image Builder = automated AMI pipeline (create → test → distribute)

Level	Instance	Subnet
Stateful?	✅ Yes	❌ No

📖 Content
🔸 Security Group (SG)

Firewall at subnet level

Rules numbered (lowest first)

🎯 Pick the Right One
Block specific IP → NACL (SG can't deny)
Allow web tier → app tier → SG referencing SG
Extra compliance layer → NACL

IAM Role	Attach via Instance Profile
IMDSv1	Simple GET (vulnerable to SSRF)
IMDSv2	Token-based (secure)
📖 Content
NEVER hardcode access keys

📖 Content

AWS Systems Manager Session Manager = browser/CLI shell to EC2.

Zero-trust architecture
Eliminates bastion hosts
Compliance-friendly

Path, host, header, query routing
WebSocket, HTTP/2, gRPC

Use: Microservices, containers (ECS/EKS)

📋 What to Learn
POLICY	WHEN TO USE

Step Scaling	Multi-threshold
Scheduled	Known time (9 AM rush)
Predictive	ML-forecast patterns
📖 Content
🔸 Components
Launch Template (preferred) — versioned, supports Spot
Min / Desired / Max capacity
Health checks (EC2 or ELB)
Multi-AZ distribution
🔸 Lifecycle Hooks

On-Demand base + Spot for cost savings
Multiple instance types for availability

📋 What to Learn
TYPE	PLACEMENT	USE CASE
Cluster	Same rack, same AZ	HPC, low latency
Spread	Distinct hardware	Critical small clusters (max 7/AZ)

📖 Content
🔸 Cluster
Lowest latency (< 1 ms)
Highest PPS
Use: HPC, distributed ML with EFA
🔸 Spread
Max 7 instances per AZ
Each on distinct hardware
Use: Critical domain controllers, master nodes
🔸 Partition
Up to 7 partitions per AZ
Use: HDFS, Kafka, Cassandra (rack-aware replication)

📋 What to Learn
IP TYPE	BEHAVIOR
Private	Permanent, free
Public	Changes on stop/start
Elastic IP (EIP)	Static, charged if unused
📖 Content
Use EIP when you need fixed public IP
Limit: 5 EIPs/region (soft)

📋 What to Learn
COMPONENT	PURPOSE
ENI	Virtual NIC
ENA	Enhanced networking (100+ Gbps)
EFA	OS-bypass for HPC/MPI/NCCL
📖 Content
🔸 ENI (Elastic Network Interface)
Virtual NIC — attach/detach from instances
Moves IP + MAC + SGs together
Use: IP failover, multi-homed EC2, MAC-tied licensing
🔸 ENA (Elastic Network Adapter)
Up to 100+ Gbps
Default on Nitro instances
Use: High-throughput workloads
🔸 EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter)
ENA + OS-bypass (via Libfabric)
Supports MPI, NCCL
Same AZ only, Cluster PG recommended

Scope	Per-AZ
HA	Deploy one per AZ
Throughput	Up to 45 Gbps
📖 Content

Single NAT GW = single-AZ failure risk

📋 What to Learn

📖 Content
🔸 Hibernation Requirements
Nitro-based instance
EBS root, encrypted
RAM ≤ 150 GB
Supported OS (Amazon Linux 2, Ubuntu, Windows)

Use Case: Apps with long warm-up (ML models, caches, JVMs) — pause overnight, resume fast.

🔸 Status Checks

CloudWatch alarm on system check → auto-recover

title: EC2 Fundamentals
body:
📘 Category 1: EC2 Instance Types — Deep Dive

Instance Family Decision Matrix (🔥 Must Memorize)

FamilyPrefixOptimized ForSAA Scenario
General PurposeT (burstable), M, A (ARM/Graviton), MacBalancedWeb apps, microservices, small-mid DBs
Compute OptimizedCCPU-intensiveGaming servers, HPC, batch, ML inference, video encoding
Memory OptimizedR, X, z1d, High Memory (u-)RAM-heavySAP HANA, Redis, Elasticsearch, real-time big data
Storage OptimizedI (NVMe SSD), D (HDD), H, Im4gn, Is4genHigh IOPS / throughputNoSQL (Cassandra), data warehouse, Hadoop, HDFS
Accelerated ComputingP (GPU ML training), G (GPU graphics), Inf (inference), Trn (training), F (FPGA)GPU/FPGAML training (P4), video rendering (G5), inference (Inf2)

Burstable vs Fixed Performance (🔥 SAA Trap)

  • T-family (T3, T3a, T4g): Baseline CPU + CPU credits. Burst above baseline consumes credits.
  • T3 Unlimited mode: Can burst indefinitely, pay extra if credits exhausted.
  • T3 Standard mode: Throttled to baseline when credits run out.

🎯 Scenario: A dev/test web server with unpredictable low traffic → T3 Standard (cheapest). A small production API with occasional spikes where performance matters more than cost → T3 Unlimited.

Graviton (ARM) Instances

  • Up to 40% better price/performance than x86
  • Instance suffix: g (e.g., m6g, c7g, r7g)
  • 🎯 Scenario: Cost-optimization question where the app is compiled for ARM (or runs on Linux/container) → Graviton.

📘 Category 2: Pricing Models — SAA Decision Logic

ModelDiscountCommitmentInterruptionExam Keyword
On-Demand0%NoneNo"Short-term, unpredictable"
Reserved Instance (Standard)~72%1 or 3 yrNo"Steady-state, known workload"
Reserved Instance (Convertible)~54%1 or 3 yrNo"Need to change family later"
Compute Savings Plan~66%1 or 3 yr ($/hr commit)No"Flexibility across EC2/Fargate/Lambda, any region/family"
EC2 Instance Savings Plan~72%1 or 3 yrNo"Specific family in region, want AZ/size flexibility"
Spot Instances~90%NoneYes (2-min warning)"Fault-tolerant, stateless, flexible start/end"
Spot Fleet / EC2 FleetMixedNoneMixed"Blend Spot + On-Demand at scale"
Dedicated HostHighest costOptionalNo"BYOL, compliance, socket/core visibility"
Dedicated InstanceModerateNoneNo"Hardware isolation, no socket visibility"
Capacity ReservationsNo discountNoneNo"Guarantee capacity in specific AZ for event"

🔥 SAA Decision Tree for Pricing

  1. Can it be interrupted? → Yes → Spot
  2. Long-term, predictable? → RI or Savings Plan
  3. Need hardware isolation + license compliance? → Dedicated Host
  4. Need guaranteed capacity for known spike? → On-Demand Capacity Reservations
  5. Mix of steady + spiky? → RI for baseline + Spot/On-Demand for spikes

🎯 Real scenario: Media company transcodes videos — each job is idempotent and retryable → Spot Fleet saves 70–90% vs On-Demand.

🎯 Real scenario: Oracle DB with BYOL requiring per-socket licensing audit → Dedicated Host (only option that exposes socket/core).

📘 Category 3: Storage — EBS, Instance Store, EFS, FSx

3.1 EBS Volume Types (🔥 Super High Exam Weight)

TypeMax IOPSMax ThroughputMax SizeUse Case
gp3 (SSD)16,0001,000 MB/s16 TiBDefault; IOPS/throughput decoupled from size. Cost-effective.
gp2 (SSD)16,000250 MB/s16 TiBOlder gen; IOPS scales with size (3 IOPS/GB)
io2 Block Express (SSD)256,0004,000 MB/s64 TiBHighest performance; SAP HANA, critical DBs
io1 / io2 (SSD)64,0001,000 MB/s16 TiBHigh-performance DBs; supports Multi-Attach
st1 (HDD)500500 MB/s16 TiBBig data, log processing, data warehouse (sequential)
sc1 (HDD)250250 MB/s16 TiBCold, infrequently accessed; cheapest

🔥 Key EBS Concepts for SAA

  • AZ-locked: EBS lives in ONE AZ. To move to another AZ → snapshot → restore in new AZ.
  • Snapshots are incremental, stored in S3 (managed by AWS, not in your bucket).
  • EBS Multi-Attach: Only io1/io2 can attach to up to 16 Nitro instances in same AZ → used for clustered apps (but app must handle concurrent writes, e.g., with cluster-aware FS).
  • Encryption: Uses KMS. To encrypt an unencrypted volume → snapshot → copy snapshot with encryption → create volume.
  • Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR): Eliminates the lazy-load penalty when restoring large volumes → critical for DR with low RTO.
  • EBS-Optimized instances: Dedicated bandwidth between EC2 and EBS.

🎯 Scenario: A MySQL DB needs 20,000 IOPS sustained → io2 (gp3 maxes at 16k). 🎯 Scenario: Restore 2 TB volume from snapshot, need immediate full performance → enable FSR. 🎯 Scenario: Shared file system across 2+ EC2 for a cluster → NOT EBS (except io2 Multi-Attach) → usually EFS.

3.2 Instance Store

  • Ephemeral NVMe SSD physically attached to host.
  • Highest IOPS/throughput available.
  • Lost on stop, hibernate, or hardware failure.
  • 🎯 Scenario: Buffer/cache for a high-performance app (e.g., Cassandra, Kafka replicas) → Instance Store (data replicated at app layer).

3.3 EFS vs FSx vs EBS (🔥 Common Exam Trap)

EBSEFSFSx for WindowsFSx for Lustre
TypeBlockFile (NFS)File (SMB)High-perf file
OSLinux/WindowsLinux onlyWindowsLinux
Multi-AZNo (AZ-locked)Yes (Regional)OptionalSingle-AZ (or Multi)
Concurrent mountsLimited (Multi-Attach)1000s of EC2ManyMany
Use caseSingle-instance diskShared Linux workloads, CMSWindows file shares, AD-integratedHPC, ML, media

🎯 Scenario: WordPress fleet across 3 AZs needing shared media files → EFS. 🎯 Scenario: Windows .NET app needing SMB share joined to AD → FSx for Windows. 🎯 Scenario: Training ML models on S3 data with ultra-low latency → FSx for Lustre.

📘 Category 4: AMI, Snapshots & Golden Images

  • AMI = EBS Snapshot + metadata + launch permissions
  • AMIs are region-scoped → copy to other regions for DR / global launches.
  • EBS-backed AMI: Root is EBS → can stop instance.
  • Instance-store-backed AMI: Root is ephemeral → cannot stop, only terminate.

EC2 Image Builder

  • Automates AMI creation, patching, testing, distribution across regions/accounts.
  • 🎯 Scenario: Enterprise wants weekly patched golden AMIs distributed to 10 accounts → EC2 Image Builder + RAM.

📘 Category 5: Networking Deep Dive

5.1 ENI, ENA, EFA

InterfacePurpose
ENI (Elastic Network Interface)Virtual NIC; can attach/detach for failover, multi-homing
ENA (Elastic Network Adapter)Enhanced networking up to 100 Gbps
EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter)HPC/ML — OS bypass, used for MPI workloads

🎯 Scenario: Tightly-coupled HPC cluster running MPI → EFA + Cluster Placement Group.

5.2 Placement Groups (🔥 SAA Favorite)

TypePlacementUse Case
ClusterSame rack, same AZLowest latency, HPC, distributed ML
SpreadDistinct hardwareSmall number of critical instances (max 7/AZ)
PartitionLogical partitions, each on separate rackBig data (HDFS, Kafka, Cassandra) — up to 7 partitions per AZ

🎯 Scenario: Cassandra cluster with 20 nodes needing rack awareness → Partition Placement Group. 🎯 Scenario: 5 critical domain controllers must never fail together → Spread Placement Group.

5.3 IP Addressing

  • Private IP: Stays with instance until terminated.
  • Public IP: Changes on stop/start.
  • Elastic IP (EIP): Static public IPv4. Free when attached to running instance; charged when unused. Limit 5/region (soft).

🎯 SAA tip: Whenever possible, avoid EIP → use ALB/NLB + DNS (Route 53) for failover, which is more scalable.

📘 Category 6: High Availability, Scaling & Load Balancing

6.1 Elastic Load Balancer (🔥 Top SAA Topic)

LBLayerProtocolsKey FeaturesScenario
ALBL7HTTP/HTTPS, WebSocket, gRPCPath-based, host-based, header-based routing; integrates with WAF, Cognito, Lambda targetMicroservices, containers (ECS/EKS), multi-tenant apps
NLBL4TCP, UDP, TLSMillions req/sec, ultra-low latency, static IP per AZ, preserves source IPGaming (UDP), IoT, financial trading, needing static IPs
GLB (Gateway LB)L3/4 (GENEVE)IPDeploys 3rd-party appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS) inlineTransparent traffic inspection via Palo Alto, Fortinet
CLB (Classic)L4/L7HTTP, HTTPS, TCPLegacy — avoid in new designsOnly for EC2-Classic

ALB Advanced Features (SAA hotspot)

  • Target types: Instance, IP, Lambda, ALB (ALB-to-ALB)
  • Sticky sessions (session affinity) via cookies
  • SNI: Multiple SSL certs on one ALB
  • Redirect HTTP→HTTPS, fixed response, authentication (OIDC/Cognito)

🎯 Scenario: Route /api/* to one target group, /images/* to another → ALB path-based routing. 🎯 Scenario: Need static IP whitelisted by customer firewall → NLB (ALB has dynamic IPs).

6.2 Auto Scaling Group (ASG) (🔥 Exam-Critical)

Core components:

  • Launch Template (preferred over Launch Configuration — supports versioning, mixed instances, Spot)
  • Min / Desired / Max capacity
  • Scaling policies

Scaling Policy Types:

TypeHow It WorksExample
Target TrackingMaintain metric at target (e.g., CPU 50%)Easiest, recommended
Step ScalingAdd N instances when CPU > X for Y minFine-grained control
Simple ScalingLegacy, one adjustment then cooldownAvoid in new designs
Scheduled ScalingScale at known time (e.g., 9 AM weekdays)Predictable traffic
Predictive ScalingML-based, forecasts and pre-scalesRecurring patterns

ASG + ELB integration:

  • ASG registers new instances with target group automatically.
  • ELB health checks can replace unhealthy instances.
  • Cooldown period prevents thrashing.
  • Warm Pool: Pre-initialized stopped instances → faster scale-out.
  • Lifecycle hooks: Run script before/after instance joins or leaves ASG.

🎯 Scenario: E-commerce during Black Friday → Predictive + Scheduled Scaling. 🎯 Scenario: Need instance to bootstrap & register with config server before serving traffic → Lifecycle hook (pending:wait).

6.3 Designing for HA

  • Multi-AZ: ASG + ELB spanning ≥ 2 AZs = baseline HA.
  • Multi-Region: Route 53 failover/latency routing + cross-region replication.
  • RTO/RPO decisions drive DR strategy:
    • Backup & Restore (hours) – snapshots to another region.
    • Pilot Light – minimal always-on in DR region.
    • Warm Standby – scaled-down active version.
    • Multi-Site Active/Active – full prod in multiple regions.

📘 Category 7: Security — SAA Focus

7.1 Security Groups vs NACLs (🔥 Recurring Trap)

FeatureSecurity GroupNACL
ScopeInstance (ENI)Subnet
StateStatefulStateless
RulesAllow onlyAllow + Deny
EvaluationAll rules evaluatedRules numbered, first match wins
ReferenceOther SGs, IPsIPs/CIDR only

🎯 Scenario: Block a specific malicious IP → NACL deny rule (SG can't deny). 🎯 Scenario: Allow web tier to talk to app tier without hardcoding IPs → SG referencing SG.

7.2 IAM Roles for EC2 (Instance Profile)

  • Credentials delivered via IMDS (Instance Metadata Service).
  • IMDSv2 (session-based, token-required) — recommended, defeats SSRF attacks.
  • Never embed access keys on instances.
